title: SPEAK-KJ – A Training Program on Dealing with Desire to Die in Pediatric Palliative Care
summary:
Overall, little is known so far about desires to die among children
and adolescents with a life-limiting illness. At the same time, studies show that children and adolescents often feel a need to talk about
their thoughts, ideas, and feelings regarding dying and death. For professionals and others who care for such seriously ill children and adolescents, it is therefore important to recognize when there is a need for conversation and to be able to conduct targeted, non-judgmental, and open discussions.
The goal of this project is to develop, implement, and subsequently evaluate a training program on addressing a desire to die in children and
adolescents for professionals in the field of hospice and palliative care. 
A review of literature will be conducted, training materials designed for adults will be analysed, and group discussions with experts will be held and analysed. This will be followed by the development and implementation of the training program. All participants will evaluate the training using a questionnaire to be completed before and after the program. If a need for change is identified, the results will be incorporated into the revision of the training materials.
conditions: Training is intended to help healthcare professionals feel more confident in dealing with a desire to die among children and adolescents in pediatric palliative care

interventions.name:
A literature review of existing research on desire to die in the field of pediatric hospice and palliative care; an analysis of existing training material from the adult sector; and focus groups with experts in pediatric hospice and palliative care.
